findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation
Upon arrival, PIC informed inspectors that the dish machine was also programmed for chemical sanitization, but the machine tested 0ppm with a chlorine test strip twice. The dish machine was observed with a final rinse temperature of 150.4F with the dish puck. The inspectors informed the PIC that the sanitizer bucket was empty and therefore not supplying the machine with chlorine for sanitization. The final rinse temperature observed is also insufficient to achieve sanitation. The chemical bucket was replaced during the inspection, but the machine failed to pull the sanitizer through the system via the pump. A follow-up is scheduled for 11/21/2025 to ensure Ecolab services and repairs the dish machine.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the lactic acid sanitizer dispenser in the dish room to measure 0ppm lactic acid with a test strip. The dispenser’s sanitizer source jug was observed to be nearly empty. If the tubing is not long enough, the sanitizer dispenser can fail before the container is fully emptied. Ensure staff are testing the dispensed sanitizer frequently and monitoring the fill level on the chemical jug. The PIC was informed of the issue and the jug was replaced, measuring 700ppm lactic acid.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Whipped butter packets were observed in pans at ambient temperature on the server line. Packets in one pan were observed with surface and internal temperatures at 64F and 60F/61F. Labeling on the box stated "Keep Refrigerated". All butter packets in question were discarded in the trash. Proper storage and use of packets were discussed, including the option of using time control for smaller portions.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41f/below at all times during storage, display and service, unless time control is used. If a time control policy is in place, then products must be labeled with the time they are pulled from proper cold holding (41F/below) and used or discarded w/in 4hrs. Establish and adhere to a policy for butter packets. 
NOTE: Wait staff must be educated on the cold holding requirement of whipped butter packets and be advised on proper storage and disposal after being out at ambient temperature (do not place packets that have been out on tables back in coolers; those packets need to be discarded).

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Portion of roast beef in gravy was observed to have surface and internal temperatures of 112F and 124F respectively. Portions were in the bottom of the warmer at the far end of the cook line. Other products in the warmer were observed at proper temperature. Manager noted the product was probably prepared around 1130a (from pre-cooked product that is heated for service). Portions were reheated to 165F prior to being placed back in the warmer for hot holding. Any leftover portions must be discarded at the end of service today.

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135F/above at all times during storage, display, and service.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Labels with names and dates for portions of food were observed on the inner surface of pans where they may come in contact with food products. Foods stored in the pans included ham and other meat in the grill cooler at the north end of the cook line. Labels are not considered a clean surface and should be placed on the outside of containers. Foods were placed in new pans with labels placed on the outside of pans.

B) A muffin baking pan was removed from a storage shelf by an employee in back prep/baking area, and the edge of the pan was tapped on the floor to remove loose crumbs from recently baked muffins. Employee and manager were advised the edge of the pan must not be touched to the floor for any reason prior to use. If the pan is to be tapped on a surface use the edge of a prep table. Also, the pans need to go through ware washing up to every 24hrs since they are used for food prep of non-potentially hazardous foods. Pan was taken to dish area to go through ware washing process.

Food and equipment must be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Ice bins at server line soda machines were observed left open between uses. Close the lids to ice bins when they are not in use to make beverages.

B) Chili and croutons were observed uncovered at soup/salad station. Lids were provided for products.

C) Foods were observed uncovered in the reach-in freezer at the north end grill line that was not currently in-use. 

D) Walnuts at the north end of the cook line were uncovered.

Foods must be properly stored and protected at all times. Cover foods when not in-use, and cover foods in coolers and freezers for long-term/overnight storage.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands without use of proper technique. Employee did not use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet upon conclusion of handwashing process. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee and management.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have become contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
findings.citation_text:
750.160 - Cook did not change gloves between tasks. Wet wiping cloth was used to wipe the front ledge of the steam table, and the employee went back to handling food without changing gloves/washing hands. Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed. Employee discarded gloves and washed hands prior to putting on a new pair of gloves and continuing with food prep. 

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task. Gloves must be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Several soiled utensils were observed hanging in the prep area available for use. Utensils went through the ware washing process and were not properly cleaned/sanitized. All soiled items were taken to the dish area to go through the ware washing process again.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.
Repeat the process as many times as necessary to remove all soil/food debris and ensure that all surfaces are properly cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sanitizer solution at 3 part sink in the dish area was observed at less then 50pm chlorine. Manager noted the solution was probably prepared this morning and had not yet been changed. Solution was emptied so the sanitize basin could be cleaned. A new sanitizer solution was prepared and observed at 50ppm chlorine.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Maintain sanitizer solution in the 3 part sink at 50-100ppm chlorine. Check the solution with test strips to verify it is at proper concentration, and change the solution frequently throughout operations depending on use and buildup of grease/soil.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - A) Damp wiping cloth was observed in a dump sink at there server line. Manager took the wiping cloth to the soiled linen storage area.

B) Wet wiping cloth was observed out on ledge of steam table on cook line. After use, it was not placed back in the sani-bucket. Proper storage of wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses was discussed with cook and manager.

C) Buckets were observed with too many wiping cloths. Several wiping cloths were piled together and not enough sanitizer solution was present to allow for submersion of cloths. Maintain an adequate amount of sanitizer solution in sani-buckets (enough to submerge cloths between uses), and do not over stock wiping cloths in solution.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces and on general surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.citation_text:
750.1320 - Bleach solution in one of the server line sani-buckets was observed to be at a concentration above 200ppm. Other sanitizer solutions were also observed to be too strong, and the bulk solution was well over 200ppm. The bulk solution was emptied to clean out the storage bin (debris/buildup observed inside). The solution was remade to be at 100ppm chlorine.

Toxic items must not be used in any manner that may present a risk of cross contamination to food, equipment, and other surfaces, nor in any manner that presents a hazard to persons that may use or come in contact with the solution. Verify the concentration with test strips, and maintain the bulk solution at 100-200ppm chlorine.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Bag of hashbrowns and boxes of sausage were observed out on the coutner at the back cookline. Manager noted products were frozen and pulled to be portioned. Items were out for ~45 minutes, which meant they were starting to thaw at ambient temperaure even though that was not the intent. Surface temperatures of sausages were below 32F, and surface temperatures of hashbrowns were at 30F-41F. Hashbrowns were immediately placed in the upright reach-in cooler. Sausages were portioned and placed in the walkin cooler.
Remove foods from cold holding units as they are ready to be used/portioned. Do not leave potentially hazardous foods out on counters for any length of time, regardless of how frozen they are.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - A) Sani-buckets in prep area and baking area tested at 0ppm chlorine. Bulk sanitizer bin was also at 0ppm. Employee in dish area stated the solution was not yet prepared. findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Portions of corn salsa positioned above fill line of a container in the top holding area of the salad cooler had surface temperatures of 51F and an internal temperature of 49F. Portions in question were discarded in the trash. Do not over-fill containers in the top holding areas of coolers. Over-filling containers results in foods in the upper portion of the containers sitting in the temperature danger zone at temperatures sometimes well above 41F.

B) Pancake batter and egg wash in the cook line cooler had surface temperatures at +50F. Internal temperatures were observed at 60F (pancake batter) and 58F (egg wash). Cook noted the foods were out for ~15 minutes. Inspector observed pancake batter being placed in the cooler upon arrival. Both products were removed from the cook line and discarded.
If it is easier to do time control, then establish and adhere to a time control policy for the in-use supplies of egg wash and pancake batter (use or discard w/in 4hrs). Otherwise, maintain cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) at 41F/below.

Cold PHF shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage. Maintain cold foods at 41F/below. If a time control policy is to be used for any in-use working supplies of PHF, then mark the time accordingly (time prepared and/or pulled from cooler) and do not use beyond the 4hr time frame for use. Discard foods after 4hrs. (this is already done for flats of eggs - establish practice for pancake batter and egg wash as well).

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - A) Pancake batter prepared at 548a today had an internal temperature of 50F when the temperature was checked after 2p. Batter was discarded.

PHF prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature (i.e. reconstituted foods, muffin and pancake mix, etc.) must be cooled to 41F/below w/in 4hrs unless time control is being used for the in-use supply of product immediately after preparation occurs.
Use ice baths to help quickly cool pancake batter. Consider portioning pancake mix in shallower pans in the walkin cooler and stir frequently to help rapidly drop the temperatures. Consolidate into a larger pan for use once pancake batter has reached 41F/below.

B) Portions of rice pilaf in the 2 door cooler had surface temperatures of 48F to 70F. Internal temperatures for portions in the middle ranged from 60F to 74F. The top layer of rice had an internal temperature around 58F-60F. According to information provided, the rice had ~20 minutes to finish reaching 41F/below for those portions that were below 70F. Top layer of rice portions were placed in the walkin cooler (temperature reached 41F w/in 20 minutes). Remaining portions were discarded in the trash. 

Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below in an additional 4hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Make sure foods have cooled adequately before portioning and stacking in a container. Plastic is an insulator and will hold heat longer. Allow rice to cool to 41F on a baking sheet (as described by manager during inspection) prior to portioning in the future.
